summary.text: A seaside links by Cynthia Dye, niece of Pete Dye, laid out over 200 hectares of dunes and coastal vegetation on Portugal's Silver Coast and opened in June 2017.

setting.text: Offers sweeping views of the Atlantic, the Berlengas Islands and the Óbidos Lagoon.
Dye said the Atlantic is visible from every hole, and that for most holes the team only had to site the greens and shape them a little: 'the course was already there waiting for us'.
Laid out as two returning loops of nine holes.
Golf Monthly's David Taylor described dramatic clifftop terrain with ocean views on every hole.
Golf Today pointed to the sea views, the colourful landscape and the elevation changes between holes.
Golf Monthly's Mike Harris said wayward drives usually get severe penalties, but forward tee options make it more playable. He heard of golfers losing a few sleeves of balls.
The clubhouse is a glass-fronted building with panoramic views of the course and the Atlantic, according to Golf Monthly's Mike Harris.

history.text: The course was around 14 years in the making before it opened.
Cynthia Dye and her team worked closely with local government agencies to keep disruption to the environment to a minimum.
It became a GEO Certified Development in its first six months.
Golf Monthly said competitors at the 2018 Portuguese Women's Amateur Golf Championship found it a tough test.
The course is managed by the nearby Praia D'El Rey resort.
Cynthia Dye is the niece of Pete Dye, the designer of TPC Sawgrass.

trivia.text: Named 'World's Best New Golf Course' at the 2017 World Golf Awards, held at La Manga Club in Spain.
It was the highest new entry, at no. 25, in a 2017 ranking of the Top 100 Courses in Continental Europe.
Golf Business News reported it as second in Top100golfcourses' list of the best courses in Portugal when it won Golf Inc.'s 2019 Golf Development of the Year award.
Golf Inc. magazine named it one of three main winners of its 2019 Golf Development of the Year awards.
In Top100golfcourses' 2026 Top 50 Golf Courses in Portugal, it sits fourth.
Golf Monthly's Mike Harris said that after playing over 500 courses worldwide, he put it in his personal top ten.
Measures 6,382 metres from the back tees, par 72.

2.text: A par 3 played from elevated tees, with a sandy waste area crossing in front of the green and bordering its right side. The resort says a constant 'swirl' affects the tee shot.

3.text: A par 4 where a tee shot down the centre lets the slope kick the ball right. A large dune on the left can block the view of the small green, which has water to its right.

5.text: A par 3 on top of a huge dune, played directly towards the Atlantic. Golf Monthly's Mike Harris said he ran out of superlatives by this hole.
The resort describes a long, redan-style green sloping front to back.

6.text: A par 5 where the resort says to avoid the right of the fairway, where large dunes block the second shot.

7.text: The second of back-to-back par 5s, with a large sandy waste area that cuts across the fairway and is hidden from the tee.

10.text: A short par 4 whose drive is partly blinded by a native sand dune that must be carried from the tee.

12.text: A par 3 to avoid on the right, where a native sandy waste bunker sits. The resort says there is a large bail-out area on the left.

13.text: A par 5 where the resort says to aim the tee shot at a natural dune bunker, and notes that there is room behind the green to tempt players into going for it in two.

16.text: A par 3 on the highest point of the course, with spectacular panoramic views.

17.text: A par 4 that doglegs around a huge dune on the right. Golf Monthly's Mike Harris said a bold line is rewarded.
The resort says the green is nestled in the pine forest at the bottom of a hill.

18.text: A par 4 played downhill from an elevated tee. Golf Monthly's Mike Harris said you can take on a dune on the left, or go right and face an approach over water.
The resort says the green is guarded by a large lake.

local.text: Lies an hour's drive north of Lisbon on the Silver Coast.
Sister course Praia D'El Rey lies about ten minutes south.
Royal Óbidos and Bom Sucesso are also in the same area.
